answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A juniper delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A nectar check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A basalt penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 1650 identities need 1650 bonds of 52 tokens, 31137 dollars of hardware and 19 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
